item.title: BOYS BASKETBALL: Elk Lake dominates Susquehanna in Division III showdown
item.description: SUSQUEHANNA – Refocused and energized, Elk Lake seized back control of the Lackawanna Division III championship race. After a pregame meeting with coach John Warnero, when he emphasized playing with a purpose, the Warriors took the court at Susquehanna High School and dominated. Chase Pond scored 28 points, John Heitsman scored 17 points, and Kendel Jones scored 13 points and collected 10 rebounds as the No. 10 Warriors posted a 69-52 win over No. 8 Susquehanna on Monday in boys basketball. item.title: BOYS BASKETBALL: Abington Heights tops Valley View for Division I crown
item.description: Jordan Shaffer had 13 points to lead four Abington Heights players in double figures, as the No. 3 Comets defeated No. 5 Valley View, 61-43, to secure the Lackawanna League Division I boys basketball title Monday night at Valley View. Finn Goldberg added 12 points, Andrew Kettel chipped in 11 points and Cooper Manning tacked on 10 for Abington Heights (16-5, 13-0). Michael Muto had 14 points to lead the Cougars (16-5, 8-5). item.title: HS SWIMMING: Lackawanna League season heads into final week
item.description: Swim teams are looking to win championships as the Lackawanna League season finishes this week. There are meets all week, starting on Tuesday, and then the competition concludes with the Les Richards Swimming and Diving Championships at Scranton High School. Elk Lake is at West Scranton at 4:30 p.m., and Wallenpaupack is at Holy Cross on Tuesday at 7 p.m. at the University of Scranton. item.title: ATHLETE OF THE WEEK: Chloe Mamera, Scranton Prep basketball
item.description: In three wins over top contenders in Lackawanna League Division I girls basketball, the Scranton Prep sophomore totaled 66 points. Mamera scored 19 points in a 46-38 victory over Scranton; 31 points in a 66-52 triumph over Valley View; and 16 points against Abington Heights in a 46-34 victory. The wins enabled the Classics to sit tied for first place with North Pocono entering the final week of the regular season. item.title: LOCAL OLYMPICS CONNECTIONS: Dallas native Radzinski trainer for U.S. Olympic ski team
item.description: A Dallas Borough native is in Italy this week to help U.S. Olympic athletes prevent injuries, manage the ones they do suffer and provide treatment as they compete to bring home the gold.
